text:
oncall-bot: INCIDENT PAGE: p99 latency spike detected for streaming endpoints in eu-west-2. SLO breach (p99 > 1200ms) and streaming stalls reported. Paging oncall.
kyle: ack - I'm on it. seeing p95 ~ 300ms, p99 ~ 1.4s on the generation cluster. Streaming tail stalls are more frequent. marking as high severity.
anika: adding telemetry: dashboards show sharp increase in TLS handshake time (~600ms->1s) and DNS timeouts for our egress NAT targets. also spike in retransmits on nodes in az-b.
rashid: checking infra - we just finished a small routing tweak earlier (route advertisement TTL adjustment) in eu-west-2 around +6m. correlates with spike start.
elaine: customer impact: 12% of streaming sessions reported stalls, 4 high-paced customers reported token stream dropouts. CS notified (lucy-cs) and sent initial template message.
lucy-cs: copying support msg sent to customer beta-2: "We're investigating intermittent streaming stalls impacting some regions; will update within 30m." Customers asking for ETA.
kyle: quick probes: curl to a streaming shard shows repeated TLS handshake retries. sample:

```
$ curl -v --max-time 10 https://stream.eu-west-2.redwood.ai/v1/stream
* Connected to stream.eu-west-2.redwood.ai (10.2.3.4) port 443 (#0)
* TLS handshake, TLS alert, Client hello (1): handshake delayed 900ms
* TLS handshake complete
> GET /v1/stream ...
< HTTP/1.1 200 OK
```

handshake latency ~900ms on many attempts.
matt-sre: kubectl logs show increased socket timeouts on inference-proxy pods in az-b. tcp_retransmit counters climbing. suspect packet loss or NAT exhaustion.
netops-bot: NAT-gw metrics: ephemeral port utilization increased to 88% on nat-gw-2; packet drops at 2.1%. New flows per second spiked after 10:12UTC.
anika: interesting - dns query latencies to resolver cluster also spiked. dig shows many SERVFAILs then timeouts. Could be dual symptom: egress NAT + resolver overload.
rashid: cross-checking control plane: no scheduler churn, nodes stable. No large deploys in the last 30m except the route tweak I mentioned.
kyle: immediate mitigations I'm trying now:
- scale up nat-gw-2 (provision extra endpoints)
- add temporary egress route to nat-gw-3 in az-c
- increase proxy keepalive to reduce new handshake churn

I'll run one change at a time and report.
elaine: prioritize customer-affecting mitigation first (reroute) before config tweaks.

kyle: applied route to nat-gw-3 via hotfix rts-20260315-1. ping tests to external resolvers improved. Handshake latencies on a sample decreased to ~300-400ms.
matt-sre: rolling restart of proxy pods in az-b to clear stuck sockets, doing 1 pod at a time.
anika: telemetry - p99 dropped from 1.4s -> 720ms after route change, still above SLO but trending down. streaming stall reports decreased from 12% -> 6% in last 5m.
lucy-cs: telling customers: "We've partially mitigated; latency reduced but we are continuing mitigation; will update in 15m." Customers appreciate the update.
rashid: netflow shows bursts of short-lived connections from our backend pool after the route change; we might still have excessive new TLS handshakes due to earlier keepalive settings.
kyle: next step: enable KV caching for certain prefix heavy endpoints to reduce traffic to inference pods (offload token generation calls). Triggered via runtime config.

```
# runtime toggle
curl -XPOST -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN" https://ops.redwood.ai/api/v1/runtime/toggle -d '{"kv_cache": "on", "target": "streaming"}'
```

oncall-bot: NOTE: all config changes logged in incident room. Correlation id: ic-4319876543
matt-sre: after cache toggle p99 to 520ms, streaming stalls now down to ~2.5% in last 3m. TLS handshake latencies still occasionally spike to ~700ms on az-b.
netops-bot: NAT-gw-2 ephemeral ports now 62% after rebalancing; packet drops down to 0.4%. DNS latency improved but occasional short spikes remain.
elaine: customer impact update for incident report: ~8% of sessions degraded total, 2 customers saw >30% request failures for <10m. No data leakage, just latency/errors. CS to offer credit if SLA hit.
lucy-cs: collecting impacted request ids and customers, will attach to post-incident report.

kyle: root cause hypothesis draft:
- initial route tweak changed next-hop behavior for some AZs -> increased flows through nat-gw-2
- nat-gw-2 reached high ephemeral port usage causing packet drops and increased TCP retransmits
- packet loss and DNS resolver overload drove TLS handshake retries -> tail latency and streaming stalls
- contributing factor: keepalive settings created more new TLS handshakes than necessary

rashid: agree. also borderline bug in egress routing table that left a minority of pods pegged to nat-gw-2 even after healthy endpoints were added.

matt-sre: long term mitigations proposed:
- fix routing behavior (ensure balanced next-hop selection) + rollout validation
- add autoscaling policy for nat endpoints based on ephemeral port usage
- lower TLS handshake churn via better keepalive defaults and connection pooling
- add runbook step to reroute traffic to alternate nat-gw on port pressure
- add more DNS resolver capacity and circuit-breaker for downstream resolvers

kyle: creating follow-up issue: INFRA-7421 (routing fix + nat autoscale). Also schedule postmortem and customer-facing incident summary.

elaine: handoff to night oncall @matt-sre in 25m. Matt, please continue watch for regressions and own the postmortem.
matt-sre: ack, will take. I'll keep the extra egress routes and KV cache toggle in place for now, will revert only after 24h of stable telemetry.

lucy-cs: final note to customers: "We have mitigated the main issues. Root cause under investigation; we'll share full postmortem and any credits required." Sending now.
oncall-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: severity -> mitigated (partial). Next update scheduled in 60m or on significant change. Incident id: ic-4319876543.
